title: Into the Woods

beats.what: Boyd and Sara make camp at the furthest point Boyd has ever reached in the forest; she is still cuffed
Kenny tells a construction crew the tower needs more material; Eric, a colony regular, is reported dead by suicide
Donna, deep in grief over Colony House's loss, takes an axe to Colony House's own floor when Kenny asks for wood for the tower
Boyd directly interrogates Sara about the voices' instructions to kill Ethan; she reveals they threatened her brother's death if she refused
Donna and Kenny argue: she says the tower will destroy people's hope when it fails; he insists they must try
Boyd and Sara discover glass bottles suspended in trees deep in the forest -- each containing a paper slip
Sara hears new voices near the bottles and collapses; after recovery she relays that a woman's voice said she was wrong and to warn Mr. Fish and Loaves
Tabitha and Jim hit what feels like the bottom of the basement dig; something breaches the hole from below

character_beats.beat: Wants to preserve what Colony House was -- a functioning community with joy -- rather than gamble it on the tower; her grief tips into sabotage then collapses into honesty with Kenny

Wants answers from the forest; walks deeper despite Sara's warning that Nathan believed pushing too hard makes the place push back -- Boyd ignores this and is rewarded with a new lead and a new terror
Discovers the power problem is solvable by tapping the town's own mysterious wiring directly -- his breakthrough shifts from ego-driven to collaborative
Optimism under resource pressure; insists the tower will work even as Kristi confronts him about the human cost of false hope

key_lines.line: They said my brother would die, okay?!
key_lines.why: Sara's motive finally stated plainly; she was not a zealot but a terrified sister -- reframes E01-E05 retroactively

key_lines.line: We're not the same people anymore.
key_lines.why: Fatima voices the season's hidden cost: even if the radio works, going home is not the same as being restored

key_lines.line: It's not a home anymore. It's a fucking tomb!
key_lines.why: Donna's Colony House epitaph; names the season's elegiac undertow -- every safe space becomes a memorial

key_lines.line: Tell Mr. Fish and Loaves that I was wrong.
key_lines.why: Message from Abby's voice (using Boyd's private military nickname) warning that deeper forces are worse than the night creatures

open_loops: What is the date 1864 on the paper slip inside the bottle, and what does it imply about how long people have been trapped here?
Who is the woman's voice Sara hears -- and why does it know Boyd by his private army nickname Mr. Fish and Loaves?
What breaches the bottom of the Matthews' basement dig in the final moments?
Are the suspended bottles a message system left by prior arrivals, or something the place itself created?
Nathan's theory was that pushing too hard makes the place push back -- does the voice warning confirm this?

payoffs.what: Fatima articulates what Tabitha's Thomas confession set up: the people here are changed in ways that make the concept of going home complicated
Jade's discovery that the town wires carry real electricity -- established in E06 with the wire-has-no-wire anomaly -- becomes the power solution for the tower

contradiction.wants: To protect the community from the crash that follows false hope -- she argues against the tower to prevent psychological damage
contradiction.does: Destroys Colony House's own floor with an axe, then privately tells Kenny she will put her game face on and support the tower, undermining her own stated position

tone_notes: The episode's central silence is its most dramatic: 141 seconds from 07:57 to 10:18 (minutes 8-10 at density 0, 0) spans the title card and fully separates the recap from the tower-construction day. It is the longest single silence in this batch. Minutes 1-2 open at a frantic 209 words -- the episode's peak -- then drop to 47 before settling into the tower-prep scenes at 90-140 range. The Donna-Kenny confrontation at minute 16 (density 139) briefly peaks before the forest scenes pull density back to the 50-115 range for much of the back half. The episode ends on an implied crescendo that the dialogue doc cannot measure: the basement breach is a silent visual shock.
